\title{Seam-Local Repair of Wavetable Wrap Discontinuities with a Self-Supervised Blended Residual}

\begin{abstract}
Wavetable synthesis exhibits cycle-boundary wrap discontinuities when stored periods do not join smoothly.
    I frame wrap repair as cycle-local seam restoration scored self-supervised via a procedural cliff-withheld sibling and a blended residual $R_{\mathrm{blend}}$.
    HybridSeam reuses genetic search, PPO, and population-based training as an engineering outer loop without claiming a new NAS or RL algorithm; confirmatory evidence is solely against neural and classical baselines (\texttt{SeamN2N}, \texttt{SeamResUNet}, \texttt{DualCosine}).
    Primary evidence is objective ($N_{\mathrm{listeners}}{=}0$; listening tests remain future work), supplemented by high-frequency click-splatter and log-spectral distortion (LSD) proxies.

    In confirmatory comparisons (Table~\ref{tab:n2n-vs-ours}, Holm--Bonferroni corrected), converged HybridSeam beats matched \texttt{SeamN2N} on $10$-seed Holdout ($0.9903$ vs $0.9764$, $p_{\mathrm{adj}}{=}0.0039$), $10$-seed Multi-family ($0.9324$ vs $0.9260$, $p_{\mathrm{adj}}{=}0.0039$), Factory+FX ($0.9108$ vs $0.8772$, $p_{\mathrm{adj}}{=}4.2{\times}10^{-15}$), and AKWF OA ($0.8740$ vs $0.8009$, $p_{\mathrm{adj}}{=}9.5{\times}10^{-21}$), remaining rank-invariant across $\alpha\in[0.3,0.9]$ and against circular Residual U-Nets ($44.5$k / $397.8$k) and a sawtooth/pulse generator ($0.9864$ vs $0.6451$).
    Across $n{=}1{,}024$ holdout evaluations, $R_{\mathrm{blend}}$ correlates negatively with $>2$\,kHz click splatter ($\rho{=}{-}0.9342$, $p{<}10^{-300}$) and LSD ($\rho{=}{-}0.6307$, $p{=}1.18{\times}10^{-114}$); on top-$10\%$ hard cliffs, Dual Cosine leaves $0.9913$ edge RMSE whereas E2 drops to $0.0086$--$0.0112$ (Table~\ref{tab:cliff-edge-rmse}).
    In $6$-seed periodic-boundary TDSE replications, $400$-step FitCell fine-tuning reaches $0.9955{\pm}0.0013$ in 1D ($p{=}0.03125$, $0.9993$ fidelity, $97.8\%$ kinetic-energy error reduction) and $0.9711{\pm}0.0044$ in 2D ($p{=}0.03125$); exploratory pilots and non-audio transfer checks are separated in Section~\ref{sec:results}.\footnote{The author used AI coding, research and writing assistants (Cursor, Grok Bot, Hermes Agent, Antigravity and SciSpace) to write code, run experiments, search and read literature, and draft and edit text. The research questions, study design and conclusions are the author's. The author checked every number against the released result files and every citation against its source, and takes full responsibility for the content. Tools used are listed in Section~\ref{sec:tooling} (Tooling and AI use).}
\end{abstract}
